building.name: North Carolina State Building Code: Building Code
building.edition: 2018 (based on the 2015 International Building Code, with state amendments)
building.local_amendments_note: Raleigh's Unified Development Ordinance adopts the state codes by reference, 'the most recent edition, including all subsequent amendments', and adds only Appendix D (Fire Districts) of the North Carolina Building Code, which is itself part of the state code. No city amendment to the building or plumbing code was found in Chapter 11 of the UDO.
building.quote: Sec. 11.1.3. Technical Codes. The term technical codes as used here shall mean the collective provisions of the North Carolina: Building, Accessibility, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Fire Prevention, Fuel Gas, Energy, Existing Buildings and Residential codes as adopted by the North Carolina Building Code Council, and the North Carolina Rehabilitation Code. The most recent edition, including all subsequent amendments, of the North Carolina Building Code, as adopted by the North Carolina Building Code Council is adopted by reference as fully as though set forth here [...] In addition, Appendix D-Fire Districts, of the North Carolina Building Code is hereby adopted by reference as fully as though set forth here and shall be enforced as part of this UDO.
building.edition_quote: The following 2018 Codes were effective from January 1, 2019 and are currently effective.
building.edition_note: The UDO names no edition; the edition and date are from the Office of State Fire Marshal's page. The city's own Special Inspections page gives 'Code Reference: 2018 NC Building Code' and 'Code Reference: 2018 NC Administrative Code' (https://raleighnc.gov/node/39751), and its commercial alteration page links the Building Code Summary Sheet to OSFM's '2018 Appendix B'.

codes.scheduled_change_note: The 2024 North Carolina State Building Code is adopted but has no start date: the Office of State Fire Marshal's page, read again on 2026-11-24, still lists the 2018 codes as currently effective and carries only the March 31, 2025 letter on the delayed effective date (state pack). Because Raleigh's ordinance adopts 'the most recent edition', the 2024 code will apply in Raleigh from the state's start date without a city vote.

fixtures.basis: Raleigh's ordinance adopts the North Carolina Plumbing Code by reference, most recent edition with all amendments, and requires plumbing fixtures to meet it. Chapter 11 of the UDO (Articles 11.1 to 11.4 read) holds no change to the toilet-count table or its rules. The city's Code Interpretation page lists only zoning interpretations, none on plumbing. The state pack's worked examples stand.
fixtures.quote: The most recent edition, including all subsequent amendments, of the North Carolina Plumbing Code, as adopted by the North Carolina Building Code Council, is hereby adopted by reference as fully as though set forth here.
fixtures.second_note: Page read through WebFetch: it names the NC Building Code, NC Fire Code and UDO, lists 'Official Zoning Code Interpretations' only (UI-1-13 to UI-1-20), and gives the chief inspectors for field interpretations, including the Chief Mechanical & Plumbing Inspector, 919-996-2449.

permit.exempt_list_quote: (c) No permit issued under Article 9 of Chapter 143 of the General Statutes is required for any construction, installation, repair, replacement, or alteration costing forty thousand dollars ($40,000) or less and performed in accordance with the current edition of the North Carolina State Building Code in any single-family residence, farm building, or commercial building unless the work involves any of the following: (1) The addition, repair, or replacement of load-bearing structures. However, no permit is required for replacement of windows, doors, exterior siding, or the pickets, railings, stair treads, and decking of porches and exterior decks that otherwise meet the requirements of this subsection. (2) The addition or change in the design of plumbing. However, no permit is required for replacements otherwise meeting the requirements of this subsection that do not change size or capacity. (3) The addition, replacement, or change in the design of heating, air-conditioning, or electrical wiring, devices, appliances, or equipment, other than like-kind replacement of electrical devices and lighting fixtures. (4) The use of materials not permitted by the North Carolina State Building Code. (5) The addition of roofing, excluding replacement. (6) Any changes to which the North Carolina Fire Code applies.
permit.city_quote: Sec. 11.4.1. Permit Requirements. Building Permit. The permit required shall conform to the provisions of the North Carolina Administration and Enforcement Requirement Code.
permit.note: Raleigh publishes no list of its own of work exempt from a permit: UDO Sec. 11.4.1 defers to the North Carolina Administration and Enforcement Requirements Code (not read), and the city's commercial alteration and repair page describes how to apply without saying which work needs no permit. The exemption is state law (G.S. 160D-1110(c), re-read on ncleg.gov on 2026-11-24). It doesn't name toilet partitions or compartments. Whether a partition replacement is a change 'to which the North Carolina Fire Code applies' (interior finish) is not stated.
permit.second_quote: Summary of the page as read through WebFetch (not a verbatim quote): how to get a permit for alterations and repairs for apartment buildings, condos, schools, restaurants, churches, mixed-use buildings and commercial projects; no statement of work that needs no permit; Permit Helpline 919-996-2500.

News and law-firm reports say Raleigh adopted Wake County's 2021 non-discrimination ordinance (in effect February 1, 2022) and that it leaves out multi-stall restrooms; the ordinance text was not read (wake.gov returned 403). This is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Raleigh job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the North Carolina rules Raleigh enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Raleigh state office buildings, university halls, schools and medical offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** North Carolina's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. Raleigh adopts them as the state writes them and enforces them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Raleigh issues building permits in Raleigh. Under North Carolina law, work in a commercial building that costs $40,000 or less needs no permit unless it involves load-bearing structure, a change to the plumbing, heating, air conditioning or electrical systems, materials the building rules don't allow, new roofing or anything the fire rules cover. The list doesn't name toilet partitions, and the city's permit pages don't say which work is exempt. Ask the city's Planning and Development Customer Service Center (919-996-2500) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** North Carolina's rules call for separate men's and women's restrooms, with signs, once a space holds more than 25 people (30 for an office, 100 for a store). Where each side needs only one toilet, two single-user rooms open to anyone may be used instead, and a family restroom doesn't have to be marked for one sex. The rules in force don't provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the City of Raleigh Planning and Development Department before planning one. State law leaves the question of who may use a multi-stall restroom to the General Assembly: state agencies, cities, counties and school boards may not set their own rules.
page.confirm_office: the City of Raleigh Planning and Development Department
page.install_rule: Commercial permits in Raleigh come from the city's Planning and Development Department. Check local contractor licensing or registration with the city before work starts. North Carolina requires a state general contractor license when the project is valued at $40,000 or more, so smaller partition jobs generally don't need one. Confirm with the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a project valued at $40,000 or more, the contractor needs a North Carolina general contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** North Carolina has no state law setting wages on public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded or assisted projects over $2,000. For a carpenter on building work in Wake County that rate is $20.48 an hour plus $3.12 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.25% in Raleigh: 4.75% state, 2% Wake County and 0.5% transit.
page.buyers_extra: - **State agencies and universities:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, with heavy-duty hardware for restrooms that see crowds between classes and sessions.
sources: - Codes enforced in Raleigh: City of Raleigh Unified Development Ordinance, Chapter 11, Building and Housing Code, [Article 11.1, Adoption of Codes by Reference](https://udo.raleighnc.gov/book/export/html/115) (Sections 11.1.3 and 11.1.4: the North Carolina Building, Plumbing and Accessibility codes, most recent edition with all amendments, adopted by reference) and [Article 11.2, Development Services Department](https://udo.raleighnc.gov/book/export/html/116); the city's [Special Inspections/Third Party Agreement](https://raleighnc.gov/node/39751) page, which cites the 2018 NC Building Code; editions and dates from the North Carolina Office of State Fire Marshal, [Codes, current and past](https://www.ncosfm.gov/codes/codes-current-and-past). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts are the state's in Raleigh: Unified Development Ordinance, [Sections 11.1.3 and 11.1.4](https://udo.raleighnc.gov/book/export/html/115), which adopt the North Carolina Plumbing Code without change; the city's [Code Interpretation](https://raleighnc.gov/permits/services/code-interpretation) page lists zoning interpretations only. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work that needs no permit: [North Carolina General Statutes 160D-1110(c)](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_160D/GS_160D-1110.html). Raleigh's permit rules: Unified Development Ordinance, [Article 11.4, Enforcement Provisions](https://udo.raleighnc.gov/book/export/html/118) (Section 11.4.1), and the city's [Commercial Alteration or Repair and Interior Completions](https://raleighnc.gov/permits/services/commercial-alteration-or-repair-and-interior-completions) page, neither of which lists exempt work; office and phone: [Planning and Development Customer Service Center](https://raleighnc.gov/permits/places/planning-and-development-customer-service-center). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Wake County: North Carolina Department of Revenue, [Current Sales and Use Tax Rates](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-rates/current-sales-and-use-tax-rates) (Wake 7.25%, including the 0.50% transit rate) and [Effective Dates of Local and Transit Sales and Use Tax Rates](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-rates/effective-dates-local-and-transit-sales-and-use-tax-rates) (2% county tax from October 1, 2009; 0.50% transit tax from April 1, 2017). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wake County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination NC20260011, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/NC20260011/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2009, through Chapter 11 of the 2018 North Carolina Building Code; 2018 North Carolina Building Code (2015 International Building Code with state amendments) and 2018 North Carolina Plumbing Code (2015 International Plumbing Code with state amendments), in force since January 1, 2019, adopted by reference in Section 11.1.3 of the City of Raleigh Unified Development Ordinance and enforced by the city's Planning and Development Department without local amendments; North Carolina General Statutes 160D-1110 for building permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE. The 2024 North Carolina State Building Code is adopted but not yet in force.

raleighnc.gov blocks curl (403) and was read through WebFetch, which summarises: the city-page quotes marked as summaries should be checked in a browser. udo.raleighnc.gov, ncleg.gov, ncdor.gov and sam.gov were read directly.

The building chapter of Raleigh's ordinance has an empty, reserved section on registering contractors, so it sets no city contractor registration; the rest of the City Code was not read, so the installation text keeps the neutral wording and the phone-call item stays open.

The 2024 North Carolina State Building Code has no start date yet; Raleigh's ordinance adopts the most recent edition automatically. When the State Fire Marshal sets a date, add a 'New rules' bullet and recheck the stall table.

News and law-firm reports say Raleigh adopted Wake County's 2021 non-discrimination ordinance and that it leaves out multi-stall restrooms; the ordinance text was not read (wake.gov blocks automated access): confirm in a browser that it holds no rule on restroom signs.
No change to Wake County's 7.25% sales tax is announced on the Department of Revenue's rate page.
The city's website names the department Planning and Development; the ordinance still says Development Services Department (as does the local-rules entry).
The buyers bullet on state agencies and universities and the four building types in the lead are editorial, not sourced.
The restroom bullet is the state pack's, with 'your local building inspections department' replaced by the City of Raleigh Planning and Development Department; the city adds no rule.
